channel.title: Cyberscoop – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Cyberscoop – Bias and Credibility (cyberscoop.com)

item.title: FBI: Iranian hackers targeting opponents with Telegram malware
item.description: Iranian government-connected groups are deploying malware via the Telegram messaging app, taking aim at dissidents and other opponents of Tehran around the world, the FBI said in an alert Friday.

item.title: State officials, election experts question California sheriff’s seizure of ballots
item.description: DEK: The attorney general has suggested the basis of the investigation and warrant stem from a rambling citizen presentation at a county meeting last month.

item.title: Experts insist Trump administration's cyber strategy is already paying off
item.description: Leaders from various cybersecurity institutions were quick to defend and evangelize the administration’s strategic pivots in cyberspace.

item.title: Russian access broker sentenced to over 6 years in prison for ransomware schemes
item.description: Russian citizen Aleksei Volkov sentenced to 81 months in prison for serving as initial access broker to Yanluowang ransomware group, facilitating attacks causing over $9 million in losses to U.S. companies.

item.title: Treasury asks whether terrorism risk insurance program should bolster cyber coverage
item.description: A Federal Register notice seeks public comment on how cyber is covered within a 2002 law and program.

item.title: Researchers say credential-stealing campaign used AI to build evasion ‘at every stage’
item.description: DeepLoad logs keystrokes, buries details behind reams of AI-generated code, and re-infect hosts days after being blocked, according to ReliaQuest.

item.title: Attack on axios software developer tool threatens widespread compromises
item.description: Researchers at numerous firms are sounding warnings about the supply-chain attack on an open-source project with 100 million weekly downloads.

item.title: White House executive order purports to limit mail-in voting, mandate federal voter lists
item.description: The order is expected to be quickly challenged in court, where the Trump administration’s previous efforts have been struck down as unconstitutional.

item.title: European-Chinese geopolitical issues drive renewed cyberespionage campaign
item.description: Proofpoint researchers say the group behind the surge, TA416, had turned away from Europe for a few years.

item.title: Medtech giant Stryker says it’s back up after Iranian cyberattack
item.description: The Handala group claimed responsibility for hitting the company with a wiper attack last month.

item.title: Lawmakers renew push for Labor Department-backed cyber apprenticeship grants
item.description: The bipartisan, bicameral Cyber Ready Workforce Act aims to cut into the country’s deficit of cybersecurity professionals.

item.title: Akira ransomware group can achieve initial access to data encryption in less than an hour
item.description: A new report from Halcyon finds that the group also puts more effort than usual into developing working decryptors, likely to incentivize businesses to pay up.

item.title: House Dems decry confirmed ICE usage of Paragon spyware
item.description: The trio of Democrats weren’t satisfied with Immigration and Customs Enforcement answers, and criticized the spyware’s use.

item.title: Wyden warns Social Security chief: Trump’s voter database is ‘blatant voter suppression’
item.description: The Senate Finance Committee Democrat said that the SSA following Trump’s executive order would indicate “willing participation” in the administration’s midterm elections scheme.

item.title: Trump budget proposal would cut hundreds of millions more from CISA
item.description: A top congressional Democrat criticized both the scope and nature of the proposed reduction.
